text:
ameya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we extract the "runtime-sheen" adapter as a first-class service to own cross-cutting transform/compat logic. Idea is small surface, high-safety cutover. Thoughts?

jordan: TL;DR what does runtime-sheen actually own vs existing request-router?

ameya: runtime-sheen would sit between the router and model runtimes. Responsibilities: 1) light canonicalization of inputs (timestamp formats, legacy fields), 2) policy-driven response shaping (truncate, map headers), 3) backwards-compatible shims for older model variants. Not runtime routing/affinity.

lia: Sounds useful. Main risk I see is splitting auth/tenant checks — we should keep auth upstream in the router. Can sheen call auth service? latency concerns.

sam: +1 to keeping auth upstream. Also: how do we avoid doubling per-request latency by inserting an extra RPC hop?

ameya: Plan: make sheen an in-process module for hotpath workers initially (feature flag), then flip to networked service when we have perf budget. That lets us iterate without immediate perf tax.

jordan: Can we do a single binary with a pluggable sheen interface first? That would preserve deployment simplicity but still model ownership.

lia: We did something similar for the encrypter sidecar. We learned in-process + config flag works well for rollout. Ops liked not having an immediate extra pod.

sam: Ops note: if we go in-process first, we need clear guardrails for memory growth. The sheen module will maintain small caches for prefix normalization. Add eviction metrics.

devon: For cutover we should have these checkpoints: 1) smoke test suite (regression prompts), 2) latency baseline run vs canary, 3) automatic rollback threshold (p95 +0.8s OR failure rate +2%). I can own the metrics dashboard.

ameya: Draft rollout steps (spike -> in-proc flag -> canary region -> global traffic):
```
# feature flag flip for dev build
SERVICE_RUNTIME_FLAGS=--sheen=inproc
# sample curl smoke test
curl -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

jordan: We also need a compatibility matrix mapping old fields -> new canonical names. That should live in the sheen repo as markdown and automated unit tests.

lia: Agreed. Also add a config-driven allowlist for shims (tenant opt-in) — enterprise customers might opt out of certain transformations.

sam: Question about observability: we should tag tokens in traces to show when sheen changed the payload. Otherwise diffs are confusing.

devon: Good call. I'll add a span "sheen.transform" and a metric sheen.transform.count with labels {tenant, transform_type}.

ameya: Policy decision: sheen won't alter auth/quotas; it can annotate payloads but not downgrade/enforce quotas. That stays in router + policy plane.

jordan: One more: tests. Add a small end-to-end harness that runs the regression prompt suite against both paths (with and without sheen) to assert semantic equivalence within config bounds.

ameya: I'll write the RFC follow-up with the plan above and link the initial checklist. @devon can you create the dashboard board and add rollback alerts?

devon: On it — will post dashboard link here when ready.

deploy-bot: Scheduled deployment window created for 2023-10-04 22:00 UTC for provisional canary cluster (sheen-inproc flag). Reminder: owners must ack 24h before.

lia: Ack from me.

jordan: Ack.

sam: Ack.

ameya: Thanks team — I'll drop the follow-up RFC and the compatibility matrix in the repo by EOD.
